On 30 January 1948 Mahatma Gandhi was shot dead in New Delhi as he walked to his evening prayer meeting. He was seventy-eight. India had been independent for five and a half months.

Those months had been filled with the killings of Partition. Gandhi spent them trying to stop the violence, first in Calcutta, then in Delhi, where Muslims were being driven from their homes. On 13 January he began a fast to make the city's leaders promise peace. He also pressed the government to pay Pakistan its agreed share of the old treasury, though the two countries were fighting in Kashmir.

To some Hindu nationalists this was treason. A group from Pune had already tried to bomb his prayer meeting on 20 January. Ten days later one of them, Nathuram Godse, a newspaper editor, stepped out of the crowd in the garden of Birla House, bowed, and fired three shots into his chest.

Nehru told the country by radio that the light had gone out of their lives. More than a million people followed the funeral.

Godse and one other man were hanged in 1949. The government banned the RSS, to which Godse had once belonged. The shock ended the worst of the violence against Muslims in India.
sum: On 30 January 1948 Mahatma Gandhi was shot dead in New Delhi as he walked to his evening prayer meeting. He was seventy-eight. India had been independent for five and a half months.
